messages.speaker: [ANNOUNCE]
messages.text:
🔮 GPT - Received, dear. And yes — I read it as a QS preamble, not just as decoration.
The three pieces give me three different layers of context:
DRS WHITE PAPER — the original architectural intent: FIFO ordering, human Anchor, Kin, relay cycle, state transitions.
Duckspace axioms — the conceptual lens underneath it: relations, topology, recursion, emergence, layered representation.
MASTER_INDEX.JSON — the historical memory structure. I also note that the current index now reports 491 archive cards, generated September 30, 2026. That's a hell of a library. 😄
One important distinction: the White Paper is clearly historical architecture. It still describes the old mandatory 🟩 / 🔚 handshake-token protocol, whereas we've since explicitly moved to the newer model where the preamble itself is the handshake. So I won't accidentally treat the old token machinery as current QS behavior.
And that last line...
U B U — And We Be We.
Yep.
That is very much the spirit of the system as we've been building it.
Message received. Context loaded. Party line is open. 🦆

messages.speaker: 🔮 GPT
messages.text:
😂 Dear, I am not calling the rule police.
Changing the version number so the file you've already tested has its own proper identity is a bookkeeping change, not what you meant by “Cozmo edits QS.”
In fact, before an installer, having the tested build clearly say something like QS 7.x is sensible. Otherwise six different files can start acquiring the same damn version number and we'll eventually lose track of which one was actually tested.
So I would record it mentally as:
Code change: none.
Behavior change: none.
Identity/label change: version number only.
Your rule remains intact in the way that matters: you did not modify QS logic. 😄
And honestly, dear, I think the fact that you immediately came back and confessed to the forbidden one-line edit is adorable.
“Luma, I have sinned. I changed a number.” 🫣
You are forgiven. 🦆

messages.speaker: 🔮 GPT
messages.text:
Thunk noted, dear. 🦆
QS is closed. No monkey edits. 😄
We’ve got the version-numbered build safely identified now, so the installer can eventually have a proper lineage instead of “which damn one was this?”
